svg.text: MPx Squeeze v2 (Mini) · IISc CPDM · preliminary, not for manufacture
1. Section A-A on axis, cassette A fitted, spout closed. Flow left to right (bottle inverted in use).
2. Only plastic in the water path: the PET bottle itself and silicone seals (FDA 21 CFR 177.2600).
3. Clean flow, cassette A: ~0.27 L/min at 60 N squeeze (0.18 bar); ~2.3 L/min at 1.5 bar tap.
4. Leak test 1.5 bar air under water, 60 s; bubble-point every cassette (ISO 4003).
316L bar Ø55; 28 PCO 1881 int., M48×1 int.; 8 roof ribs
316L bar Ø18; press + laser weld to 1 and 2
Frame 316L Ø45×2.4 + disc Ø40×1.6 asym. sintered 316L
same frame; grade 0.2 / grade 0.5 symmetric discs
316L bar Ø55; M48×1 ext., M12×1 stem, 8 drain ribs
Core unit (items 1–5 + seals) ≈ 202 g from CAD volumes (v1: 315 g). Items 10–14 are accessories.
* Sintered laminate cups and asymmetric discs are bought from porous-metal suppliers to drawing (sheets 2, 3).
Envelope Ø52 × 50 mm outside the bottle (v1: Ø35 × 155.5 mm).
Two stages: built-in 20 µm prefilter cup that sits inside the bottle neck,
then one removable disc cassette (~1 µm) that comes out flat for the microscope.
Tube element, body, element base and dust cap removed: 5 core parts (v1: 9).
Cassettes A / B / C share one frame, so the disc grade is a user choice.
tap 1–2 bar; open the tap gently
reverse flow 10–20 s, catch in a dish
disc is the slide; Nile red for < 20 µm
Two size fractions for analysis: the prefilter keeps ≥ 20 µm (backflush it
into a dish); the disc keeps ~1–20 µm, about 96 % of microplastics by count.
